tools.name: stack_analyze
tools.description: Check a list of dietary supplements for a person: per-nutrient daily totals against NIH upper limits (UL) and RDA/AI, which products overlap, what each UL protects against, and single-product changes that would bring an above-UL nutrient back under it. Products can be given as names ("Centrum Silver

tools.name: products_search
tools.description: Search the NIH Dietary Supplement Label Database by product name, brand or ingredient. Returns up to 10 products (one per product; older label versions listed in other_versions) with DSLD IDs.

tools.name: products_lookup
tools.description: Look up a supplement by the UPC/EAN barcode printed on the bottle. Returns the newest matching DSLD label, normalized, and any older versions.

tools.name: products_get
tools.description: Full normalized supplement labels by DSLD ID (up to 10): every ingredient with label amount, converted amount, form and %DV.

tools.name: interactions_check
tools.description: Which vitamins and minerals interact with given medications (generic or brand names, e.g. "warfarin", "Synthroid") or conditions, per the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets, with timing advice (e.g. take levothyroxine 4 hours apart from calcium). No product list needed; to check an actual

tools.name: products_fda_reports
tools.description: FDA recalls and adverse event reports (CAERS) for one supplement, from openFDA. Give a product name, barcode, DSLD ID, or brand and name. Recalls are listed only when they carry the barcode or the brand and every product-name word; adverse event reports are counted with their most common reactions.

tools.name: nutrients_reference
tools.description: NIH reference values (RDA, EAR, AI, UL) for one vitamin or mineral at a given age and sex, with what the UL protects against. Offline and instant.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "products_fda_reports" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.
